_note: How a services firm commercialises a Lyzr product. The second half of discovery: the capability path asks what work a partner could sell next, this one asks which Lyzr product their existing business is already shaped to resell, deploy or run. Every `capabilities` line is read off the product's own page; nothing here is written from memory. `requires` is the gate: a play may only be proposed when the partner's capability map actually shows that signal, because an industry match is not a reason to recommend a product.

plays.name: OpenController
plays.one_line: The control plane over every agent a client is already running, wherever it runs.
capabilities: Discovers agents across clouds, clusters and on-premises, including ones nobody registered
Issues workload identity to every agent through the client's existing identity provider
Enforces policy in the request path: access control, rate limits, model routing and guardrails
Gates releases on multi-turn, red-team and regression evals with evidence per version
Traces every action with cost, quality and ownership, exported to their observability tools
complements: Agent or GenAI delivery work already in production at clients
Cloud platform engineering and landing zone work
Security, identity or compliance practices

requires.why: A control plane is only sellable to a firm whose clients already have agents running, or who runs the platform those agents would run on.

implementation.offer: Find every agent the client is running, put identity and policy on each one, and hand back an inventory with an audit trail

managed.offer: Run the control plane for them: policy changes, release gating and the evidence pack their risk function asks for

plays.buyer: CISO, Head of Platform Engineering or Chief Risk Officer
plays.trigger: Agents are in production that nobody has inventoried, or an audit date is on the calendar
prerequisites: The client has agents running somewhere, built on anything
An existing identity provider to authenticate against
Someone accountable for AI risk
do_not_recommend_when: The partner has never delivered anything into production for a client
Their clients have no agents and no plan for any, so there is nothing to govern
The partner only advises and does not operate anything

plays.name: Open Cowork
plays.one_line: A governed AI coworker for every employee, rolled out across a workforce rather than built per use case.
capabilities: Gives every employee an AI coworker inside the organisation's own governance
Deployed across a workforce rather than built one use case at a time
complements: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or intranet rollouts
Employee experience, adoption and change programmes
Service desk and internal support work

requires.why: Rolling an AI coworker out to a whole workforce is an adoption and change programme. A firm that has never run one has no business selling it.

implementation.offer: Stand it up for one department, agree what good looks like, then roll it out across the workforce

managed.offer: Run adoption, policy and the content behind it, billed per seat per month

plays.buyer: Chief Information Officer, Head of Digital Workplace or Chief People Officer
plays.trigger: Staff are using consumer AI tools the organisation cannot see, or a workforce AI policy has just been written
prerequisites: A single sign-on directory covering the workforce
Somebody who owns employee tooling and can mandate it
An acceptable use position on AI
do_not_recommend_when: The partner has no record of workforce rollouts or adoption work
Their clients are small enough that a per-seat rollout is not a programme
The partner sells only to engineering teams, not to the business

plays.name: Agent Studio
plays.one_line: The pro-code workbench an engineering team designs, tests and ships production agents from.
capabilities: Design, test and ship production agents from one place
Carries the workflow and the integrations rather than leaving them to be stitched together
complements: Custom software and application development
Data engineering and integration work
Existing AI or ML delivery teams

requires.why: A build platform is sold to a firm that builds. An advisory firm has nobody to put on it.

implementation.offer: Build the first agent on the client's own workflow, in production, then repeat the pattern

managed.offer: Run and extend what was built, billed monthly rather than re-quoted per change

plays.buyer: VP Engineering, Head of Data or Chief Technology Officer
plays.trigger: They have agent prototypes that have not reached production, or every new use case is being rebuilt from scratch
prerequisites: Engineers the partner can put on delivery
Access to the systems the agents have to read and write
do_not_recommend_when: The partner only advises and subcontracts all delivery
They already run a build platform of their own that they sell

plays.name: Architect
plays.one_line: Business users describe an agent or an app and it gets built, with the partner's agents coming along too.
capabilities: Build agents and apps in one flow, including by describing them
Bring existing agents with you rather than rebuilding them
complements: Process improvement and operating model work
Low-code and RPA practices
Business analysis teams sitting close to the client

requires.why: This is sold into the business, not into engineering. The partner has to already be in the room where processes are decided.

implementation.offer: Map the process with the people who run it, then build the first app with them in the room

managed.offer: Keep the apps current as the process changes, billed monthly

plays.buyer: Chief Operating Officer or a function head who owns the process
plays.trigger: A backlog of small automations nobody will fund individually, or an RPA estate that keeps breaking
prerequisites: Named business owners for the processes in scope
The partner has access to the business, not only to IT
do_not_recommend_when: The partner sells only to engineering teams
The work in question genuinely needs a pro-code build

plays.name: SuperFlow
plays.one_line: Visual workflow orchestration with durable execution, so the flow that worked in the demo survives production.
capabilities: Visual workflow building for agents, LLM pipelines, approvals and long-running processes
Durable execution: every step is journaled and a restart resumes from the point of failure
Structured approvals with typed fields and files flowing on through the workflow
Enterprise connectivity built in: OAuth2 with refresh, AWS Signature v4, JWT and mTLS
Hybrid orchestration that brings existing agents forward alongside new ones
complements: Integration and middleware practices
Workflow and BPM work
Existing RPA or iPaaS estates

requires.why: Durable orchestration is sold to a firm that already owns the client's process plumbing. Without that they are selling a canvas.

implementation.offer: Rebuild one brittle long-running workflow on durable execution and show it surviving a failure

managed.offer: Own the orchestration layer and the runbook, billed per workflow per month

plays.buyer: Head of Integration, Head of Automation or an operations director
plays.trigger: A workflow that works in testing keeps failing in production, or approvals are being handled over email beside the system
prerequisites: Processes long enough or branching enough to need orchestration
Access to the systems each step has to call
do_not_recommend_when: The work is a single model call with no steps around it
The partner has no integration or process practice to attach it to

plays.name: Lyzr Optimus
plays.one_line: Lyzr's own appliance: agents, models and governance running inside the client's data centre, air-gapped.
capabilities: Runs open-weight models entirely on-premise with no external calls
Agents operate in air-gapped environments without network connectivity
Fixed annual pricing rather than per-token metering
Custom models and fine-tunes can be imported for specialised use
complements: Data centre, private cloud and on-premise infrastructure work
Sovereignty, residency and classified environment delivery
Hardware procurement and installation practices

requires.why: An appliance is sold by firms that already put equipment into other people's data centres. A cloud-only consultancy cannot deliver it.

implementation.offer: Install and commission the appliance in their environment, with the first workload running on it

managed.offer: Operate the appliance under an SLA: patching, model updates and capacity, billed annually

plays.buyer: Chief Information Security Officer, Head of Infrastructure or a programme director in a regulated body
plays.trigger: Data is not permitted to leave the estate, or per-token cost on an existing deployment has become unpredictable
prerequisites: Somewhere to physically put it, with power, cooling and network
The partner can deliver into a client data centre
A workload that genuinely cannot go to a public cloud
do_not_recommend_when: The partner has only ever delivered in public cloud
Their clients have no residency or sovereignty requirement
The timeline is immediate: it ships Q4 2026

plays.name: AgentBlocks OEM
plays.one_line: White-label agent platform infrastructure a software vendor ships inside their own product, under their own name.
capabilities: White-labeled build, governance and runtime layer for an agent platform
Tenant isolation, request isolation, environment separation and durable execution
Deployment into customer VPC, private cloud, Kubernetes or on-premises
Audit logs, approvals, policy enforcement, usage metering and tenant limits
Adapters onto existing frameworks, models, cloud, IAM, CI/CD and telemetry
complements: An existing product with its own customers and its own release cycle
Multi-tenant SaaS platforms
Vertical software with a captive install base

requires.why: This is sold to a firm that ships software of its own. A pure services business has no product to embed it in.

implementation.offer: Embed the runtime behind their own product's brand and ship agent features to their existing customers

managed.offer: Lyzr carries the platform layer underneath while they own the product, the roadmap and the customer

plays.buyer: Chief Product Officer, Chief Technology Officer or a general manager who owns the P&L for the product
plays.trigger: Customers are asking the product for AI features, and building the platform layer underneath would take a year
prerequisites: A product of their own that customers already pay for
An engineering team that can integrate an SDK
A commercial model that can carry a platform cost
do_not_recommend_when: The partner sells only people and hours, with no product of its own
They already own a mature agent platform they sell
What they actually need is a single agent, not a platform underneath one

plays.name: Agent Blocks
plays.one_line: The primitives underneath, memory, tools, retrieval and orchestration, composed into something the partner is already building.
capabilities: Memory, tools, retrieval and orchestration as composable primitives
Used piece by piece inside work the partner is already delivering
complements: An agent or application the partner is already building for a client
Existing frameworks they do not want to replace

requires.why: Primitives are for a team that is building something of their own. There is nothing to compose them into otherwise.

implementation.offer: Replace the part they are hand-rolling, memory or retrieval, in one build and measure what it saves

managed.offer: Keep the primitives current underneath their builds as models and tooling move

plays.buyer: Engineering lead or solution architect on the delivery team
plays.trigger: They are maintaining their own memory, retrieval or orchestration code and it is drifting behind the model releases
prerequisites: An active build, not a greenfield intention
Engineers who will work against an SDK
do_not_recommend_when: The partner wants a platform rather than parts: that is AgentBlocks OEM, which is a different conversation
They are not building anything themselves

plays.name: Open Finetuning
plays.one_line: Fine-tune open-weight models on the client's own data, inside the client's own environment.
capabilities: Fine-tune open-weight models on the client's own data
complements: Data engineering and feature pipelines
Existing machine learning practices
Sovereignty and residency work

requires.why: Fine-tuning is sold by firms with data science people. Without them the engagement has nobody to run it.

implementation.offer: Fine-tune on one corpus the client owns and measure it against the general model on their own examples

managed.offer: Retrain and re-evaluate on a schedule as the client's data moves

plays.buyer: Head of Data Science or Chief Data Officer
plays.trigger: A general model is not good enough on their domain language, or their data cannot be sent to a vendor
prerequisites: Enough labelled or structured data of their own
Somewhere to run the training
A measurable task to improve
do_not_recommend_when: The partner has no data science capability of its own
Prompting and retrieval would get them there without training anything
